name: Nimesulide
restricted_in: India (banned for children under 12, restricted use in adults)
reason: Hepatotoxicity (severe liver damage) risk. Never approved by FDA in the US; restricted for pediatric use in India since 2011.

name: Analgin (Metamizole / Dipyrone)
reason: Risk of agranulocytosis (life-threatening drop in white blood cells). Banned in India in 2013; never approved in the US.

name: Furazolidone
restricted_in: USA (withdrawn from human use, veterinary restrictions)
reason: Carcinogenicity concerns and drug interaction risks (MAOI-like effects).

name: Phenylpropanolamine (PPA)
reason: Increased risk of hemorrhagic stroke, particularly in women. FDA requested withdrawal in 2000; banned in India in 2011.

name: Sibutramine
reason: Increased risk of cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke). Withdrawn from US market in 2010; banned in India in 2011.

name: Rofecoxib
reason: Significantly increased risk of heart attack and stroke. Voluntarily withdrawn worldwide by manufacturer in 2004.

name: Cisapride
reason: Serious cardiac arrhythmias (QT prolongation), some fatal. Withdrawn from general US market in 2000.

name: Gatifloxacin (oral/systemic)
restricted_in: USA (oral form discontinued; ophthalmic form still available)
reason: Severe blood glucose disturbances (hypo/hyperglycemia). Oral systemic form banned in India in 2011.

name: Valdecoxib
reason: Increased cardiovascular risk and serious skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome). Withdrawn in 2005.

name: Pioglitazone
banned_in: India (temporarily banned in 2013, later reinstated with warnings)
reason: Increased risk of bladder cancer and heart failure. Briefly banned in India in 2013; currently allowed with restrictions/warnings.

name: Terfenadine
reason: Serious cardiac arrhythmias, especially with certain drug interactions. Withdrawn from US market in 1998, replaced by fexofenadine.

name: Nitrofurazone
reason: Carcinogenicity concerns based on animal studies.
